title: Deadlock or Safe?
prompt: Implement `const char *lock_verdict(int kind)`: 0 two threads acquire mutexes A then B, and B then A → a deadlock risk; 1 all threads acquire A then B → safe; 2 second lock taken with try-lock, released and retried on failure → safe; 3 blocking acquisition of a second lock while an outer lock is held by the same thread that another thread needs first → a deadlock risk; 4 a single mutex, no nesting → safe.

tests.name: inversion is the risk
tests.hint: Opposite acquisition orders can form a cycle: the definition of a deadlock risk.

tests.name: consistent order is safe
tests.hint: A global order (or a single lock) cannot cycle.

tests.name: try-lock escapes
tests.hint: try-lock converts deadlock into retry; blocking second acquisition while holding the first keeps the risk.
